title: HTML and CSS reference
summary: Tags and CSS you can click to insert, with what each one does.

items.label: <h1> heading
items.hint: The biggest heading. Use it once for the page title.
items.shows: The biggest heading

items.label: <h2> subheading
items.hint: A smaller heading for a section.
items.shows: A smaller heading under the title

items.label: paragraph
items.hint: A paragraph of text.
items.shows: Two paragraphs, with a gap between

items.label: <div> box
items.hint: A container that groups things together, so you can style them as one.

items.label: <ul> list
items.hint: A bulleted list. Each item is an <li>.
items.shows: A bullet for each <li>

items.label: <ol> numbered list
items.hint: A numbered list.
items.shows: The browser numbers the items

items.label: comment
items.hint: A note that the browser ignores.
items.example: You can see this.
items.shows: The comment does not show

items.label: <a> link
items.hint: A link. The address goes in href; the words between the tags are what people click.
items.shows: The link text is blue and underlined

items.label: image
items.hint: A picture. src is the picture file; alt describes it for people who cannot see it. There is no closing tag.
items.example: Second place
items.shows: The picture, 100 pixels wide

items.label: <strong> bold
items.hint: Make text stand out as important (usually bold).
items.shows: Only the word inside is bold

items.label: <em> emphasis
items.hint: Emphasise text (usually italic).
items.shows: Only the word inside is italic

items.label: <button>
items.hint: A button.
items.shows: A button (clicking does nothing yet)

items.label: line break
items.hint: Start a new line.
items.shows: A new line inside one paragraph

items.label: <hr> line
items.hint: Draw a line across the page.
items.shows: A line across the page

items.label: <table>
items.hint: A table: <tr> is a row, <th> a heading cell, <td> a normal cell.
items.shows: Headings in bold, one row per <tr>

items.label: <header>
items.hint: The top part of a page: usually the title and the menu. Looks like a div; the name tells browsers and screen readers what it is.
items.shows: It looks like any block: the name is the difference

items.label: <nav>
items.hint: The main menu of links.
items.shows: A group of menu links

items.label: <main>
items.hint: The main content of the page. One per page.
items.shows: The main content

items.label: <section>
items.hint: One part of the page, usually with its own heading.
items.shows: One part of a page with its heading

items.label: <footer>
items.hint: The bottom part of a page: contact details, small print.
items.shows: The bottom of the page

items.label: page parts
items.hint: The parts of a page, named: header, nav, main with its sections, and footer. They look like plain blocks; the names are for screen readers and search engines.
items.example:
Chess club

  • Home
  • Rules

When we meet

Wednesdays at lunch.

Contact the teacher in charge.
items.shows: Each part is a plain block: the tag names are the difference

items.label: jump link
items.hint: A link to a place on the same page. id names the place; href starts with # and the same name.
items.example:
• Results
  • Join

Results

The Owls won.

Join

Come on Wednesday.
items.shows: Clicking a link scrolls the page to its heading

items.label: <form>
items.hint: Holds the fields and the button that sends them. On its own, a form sends nowhere: code behind it does the work.
items.shows: A field and a button

items.label: label and input
items.hint: An input is a box to type in. Its label says what to type; for and id must match, so clicking the label puts the cursor in the box.
items.shows: A labelled box for a number

items.label: <select> drop-down
items.hint: A drop-down list: one option to choose.
items.shows: A drop-down showing its first option

items.label: <style> block
items.hint: Where CSS lives. Each rule is: selector { property: value; }
items.shows: The rule styles every <h2>

items.label: rule
items.hint: Style every element matching the selector.
items.shows: Every <li> is teal

items.label: class selector
items.hint: Style only the elements you mark with class="note" in the HTML. The dot is only in the CSS.
items.example:
A normal paragraph.

A paragraph with class="tip".
items.shows: Only the paragraph with the class changes

items.label: several selectors
items.hint: One rule for several kinds of element: list the selectors with commas.
items.example:
Title

  • An item

A paragraph
items.shows: The heading and the list item change; the paragraph does not

items.label: color
items.hint: The text colour.
items.shows: Text colour

items.label: background-color
items.hint: The background colour.
items.shows: The colour behind the text

items.label: font-size
items.hint: How big the text is.
items.shows: A bigger heading

items.label: font-family
items.hint: Which font to use.
items.shows: A different font

items.label: text-align
items.hint: Align text: left, center or right.
items.shows: The heading moves to the middle

items.label: display: flex
items.hint: Put it on the box that holds the items (the parent): its children line up in a row.
items.shows: The three paragraphs sit side by side

items.label: gap
items.hint: Space between the items in a flex row (on the parent, with display: flex).
items.shows: 40 pixels between the items

items.label: flex-wrap
items.hint: Let items move to the next line when the row is full.
items.shows: The fourth star wraps to the next line

items.label: justify-content
items.hint: Where the items sit along the row: flex-start, center, flex-end or space-between.
items.example:
Left

Right
items.shows: space-between pushes the items to the ends

items.label: list-style
items.hint: Remove the bullets or numbers from a list: menus are lists without bullets.
items.shows: A list with no numbers

items.label: display: grid
items.hint: Put it on the box that holds the items: its children are placed in rows and columns (with grid-template-columns).
items.example:
A

B

C

D
items.shows: Four boxes in two columns

items.label: grid-template-columns
items.hint: The width of each column, in order. 1fr means one share of the space left; repeat(3, 1fr) makes three equal columns.
items.example:
80px
The rest
items.shows: A fixed column, then one that takes the rest

items.label: width
items.hint: How wide the content is. Padding and border are added on top of it.
items.example: A box 120 pixels wide
items.shows: The box is 120 pixels wide

items.label: padding
items.hint: Space inside an element, between its edge and its content.
items.shows: Space between the edge and the text

items.label: margin
items.hint: Space outside an element, between it and its neighbours.
items.shows: Space around each box

items.label: border
items.hint: A line around an element: thickness, style, colour.
items.shows: A line around the paragraph

items.label: menu links
items.hint: Style only the links inside the nav. The space means inside: nav a is every a within a nav.
items.example:
• Home
  • Rules

A link in the text keeps its look.
items.shows: The menu links change; the link in the text does not

items.label: card box
items.hint: A box with room inside (padding), a line around it (border) and space outside it (margin). Width sets the content only.
items.example:
Chess

Wednesdays at lunch.
items.shows: A card 200px wide inside, 244px with its padding and border

items.label: flex row
items.hint: A row of items. gap is the space between them, justify-content places them along the row, align-items lines them up across it.
items.example:
Chess club

Join us
items.shows: The title on the left and the text on the right, lined up across

items.label: wrapping row
items.hint: A row that moves items to a new line when there is no room. flex: 1 lets items share the space and min-width stops them getting too narrow.
items.example:
One

Two

Three

Four
items.shows: Items share the row, then wrap when the preview is narrow

items.label: card component
items.code:
‹

Title

› ‹

Some text.

›
items.hint: A chunk of HTML with a class. Copy the section for each card; one rule styles every copy.
items.example:
Chess

Wednesdays.

Art

Thursdays.
items.shows: Two cards, one rule

items.label: on click
items.hint: When the element with id="go" is clicked, run the lines inside. # means id, as . means class.

items.label: change the text
items.hint: Replace the words inside the element with id="message".

items.label: read a box
items.hint: Read what someone typed into the box with id="name".

items.label: Bootstrap link
items.hint: Loads Bootstrap's stylesheet: a big CSS file someone else wrote. Put it first, above your own <style>. On your own site, download it from getbootstrap.com and put it beside your page.

items.label: container
items.hint: A centred column with space at the sides. Most Bootstrap pages put everything inside one.

items.label: btn button
items.hint: btn gives the button shape; a second class picks the colour: btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-success, btn-danger, btn-warning, or btn-outline-primary for an outline. Add btn-lg or btn-sm for the size. It needs both btn and a colour.
items.example:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="bootstrap.min.css">

<button class="btn btn-primary">Save</button>
<button class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Cancel</button>
<button class="btn btn-danger btn-sm">Delete</button>
items.shows: Three buttons: blue, outlined and a small red one

items.label: alert
items.hint: A coloured message box. alert gives the box; alert-primary, alert-success, alert-danger, alert-warning or alert-info picks the colour.
items.example: The library is open at lunch.
items.shows: A light blue message box

items.label: spacing and text classes
items.hint: m is margin and p is padding; then t, b, s, e (top, bottom, start, end), x (both sides) or y (top and bottom), then a size from 0 to 5: mt-3 is a space above. text-center centres text; lead makes a larger opening paragraph; fw-bold makes it bold.
items.example:
Welcome!

A box with space above and padding inside.
items.shows: A large centred line, then a padded box lower down

items.label: navbar
items.code:
‹Club name›
  • ‹Link›
items.hint: The bar across the top: the brand (your name) on the left, then the menu. navbar-expand keeps the menu in a row (folding it into a button on phones needs Bootstrap's JavaScript).
items.example:
Library
  • Books
  • Hours
items.shows: A grey bar with a name and two menu links

items.label: card
items.hint: A box with a border and rounded corners. The card-body inside gives it padding; card-title and card-text style what is in it.
items.example:
Robotics

Fridays in the lab.
items.shows: A bordered box with a title and a line of text

items.label: row and col
items.hint: Bootstrap's grid: a row lines up the cols inside it, and each col takes an equal share. col-4 and col-8 split the row 4 to 8 (a row is 12 parts). Put a row inside a container.
items.example:
One
Two
Three
items.shows: Three boxes sharing a line equally

items.label: form-control
items.hint: Bootstrap's look for a form: form-label on each label, form-control on each box, form-select on a drop-down. The for and id still link them.
items.shows: A label above a full-width box

items.label: table class
items.hint: Bootstrap's look for a table: lines between rows and padding in the cells. table-striped shades every other row; table-bordered adds borders.

items.label: Bulma button
items.hint: Bulma works like Bootstrap with different names: button for the shape, is-primary, is-success or is-danger for the colour, is-large for the size.
items.shows: Two Bulma buttons

items.label: Tailwind utility classes
items.code:
<script src="tailwind.js"></script>
<button class="‹bg-blue-600 text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-lg›">‹Join›</button>
items.hint: Tailwind has one class per CSS property: bg-blue-600 is the background, text-white the text colour, px-4 and py-2 the padding, rounded-lg the corners. Here tailwind.js writes the CSS as the page loads (for trying things); real sites use a build tool.
items.example: Sale today!
items.shows: A yellow box with large bold text

items.label: daisyUI button
items.hint: daisyUI puts Bootstrap-style names (btn, card, alert) on top of Tailwind, so you can mix whole parts with Tailwind's one-property classes.
items.shows: A daisyUI button

items.label: Pico (no classes)
items.hint: Pico's classless version styles plain tags: a page with headings, paragraphs, forms and buttons looks tidy with no class names at all. Put the page in a <main>.
items.shows: A heading and a button, styled with no classes

items.label: Vue app
items.code: ‹the page›
items.hint: Vue looks after everything inside the div with id app. setup makes the data and functions, and returns the names the page can use. vue.js sits beside the page.
items.example: Today: {{ temp }} °C
items.shows: A sentence showing the data: Today: 21 °C

items.label: ref data
items.hint: Data that Vue watches: when it changes, the page follows. Return it from setup. In the script its value is score.value; on the page, just score.

items.label: show data {{ }}
items.hint: Shows a value from setup on the page, and keeps it up to date. Any short expression works: {{ score * 2 }}.

items.label: @click event
items.hint: Runs a function from setup when the button is clicked. A short change works too: @click="score++".

items.label: v-for
items.hint: Makes this tag once for each item in the list. Put it on the tag you want more of (the li, not the ul).
items.example: • {{ fruit }}
items.shows: A list with one item for each fruit

items.label: v-if
items.hint: Shows the tag only while the condition is true. v-else on the next tag shows when it is false.

items.label: v-model
items.hint: Joins a box to a ref, both ways: typing changes the data, and changing the data changes the box. On a tick box it is true or false.

items.label: function in setup
items.hint: A function the page can run (return it from setup). In the script, a ref's value is in .value.

items.label: computed
items.hint: A value worked out from other data. Vue works it out again whenever that data changes, so it never goes stale. Never set it yourself.

items.label: component and props
items.hint: A tag of your own, made once and used many times: <player-card :name="p.name"></player-card>. The colon passes a value. Make the app with const app = createApp(...), add components, then app.mount("#app").

items.label: Preact app
items.hint: Preact works like React. A component is a function that returns its page, written in html`…` (htm). Preact runs the function again after every change.

items.label: useState
items.hint: Preact and React state: the value, and a function to change it. Always give it a new value: setStars([...stars, item]), never stars.push.

items.label: Svelte component
items.code:
<textarea data-svelte hidden>
  <script>
    ‹state and functions›
  </script>
  ‹the page›
</textarea>
<script src="svelte.js"></script>
items.hint: Here a Svelte component sits in a hidden textarea and svelte.js compiles it in the page. In a real project it is its own file, App.svelte.
items.shows: Hello, world!

items.label: $state and $derived
items.hint: Svelte's data that changes, and a value worked out from it. Change $state data directly (count++, list.push). Show it with {count}; choose with {#if …} … {/if}.

items.label: fetch JSON
items.code:
const response = await fetch("‹weather.json›");
const data = await response.json();
items.hint: Asks for a file or web address, waits for the reply, then turns it into data (objects and arrays). Both lines need await, inside an async function.
items.example: Loading…
items.shows: Loading… becomes Days: 7 once the file has arrived

items.label: async function
items.hint: A function that may wait for slow things with await. Call it like any function; the rest of the page keeps going while it waits.

items.label: try and catch
items.hint: Runs the lines in try; if one fails (no network, a blocked site), jumps to catch instead of stopping with an error.

items.label: alt text
items.hint: Says what a picture shows, for anyone who can't see it (screen readers read it aloud). Use alt="" for a picture that is only decoration.

items.label: heading outline
items.code:
‹Page title›

‹A part of the page›

‹A part of that part›
items.hint: Headings are the page's outline: one h1, then h2 for each part, h3 inside those. Never pick a level for its size; set the size with CSS.

items.label: whole page
items.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>‹My page›</title>
</head>
<body>
  ‹the page›
</body>
</html>
items.hint: What a page file needs around its content: the language, the text encoding, a phone-friendly width and a title for the tab. The Download button adds it for you.

items.label: relative path
items.hint: A file name with no folder means "beside this page"; images/trophy.svg means "in the images folder beside this page". Never a path from your own computer (C:/Users/…).
